drivingQuestion: What does one who gladdens a groom earn, and are the voices at Sinai really only five?
outcomeNote: The contradiction against the count of five voices is answered — the extra voices preceded the giving of the Torah. The reward question ends with three answers standing side by side, each read out of a further clause of Jeremiah 33:11.

segments.he: וְאָמַר רַבִּי חֶלְבּוֹ, אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: כׇּל הַנֶּהֱנֶה מִסְּעוּדַת חָתָן וְאֵינוֹ מְשַׂמְּחוֹ עוֹבֵר בַּחֲמִשָּׁה קוֹלוֹת, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״קוֹל שָׂשׂוֹן וְקוֹל שִׂמְחָה קוֹל חָתָן וְקוֹל כַּלָּה קוֹל אוֹמְרִים הוֹדוּ אֶת ה׳ צְבָאוֹת״.
segments.en: «And Rabbi Ḥelbo said» that «Rav Huna said: Anyone who benefits from the feast of a groom but does not cause him to rejoice violates the five voices» mentioned in this verse, «as it is stated: “The voice of joy and the voice of gladness, the voice of the groom and the voice of the bride, and the voice of those who say: Give thanks to the Lord of hosts,» for the Lord is good, for His mercy lasts forever, even of those who bring a thanks-offering to the house of the Lord. For I will restore the captivity of the land as it was in the beginning, says the Lord” (Jeremiah 33:11). These five voices in the context of a bride and groom correspond to the five voices mentioned in the context of the revelation at Sinai, as in Song of Songs, the day of the revelation at Sinai is alluded to by the phrase: His wedding day (Rabbi Yoshiyahu Pinto, Maharsha).

segments.he: וְאִם מְשַׂמְּחוֹ מַה שְּׂכָרוֹ? אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי: זוֹכֶה לַתּוֹרָה שֶׁנִּתְּנָה בַּחֲמִשָּׁה קוֹלוֹת, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וַיְהִי בַיּוֹם הַשְּׁלִישִׁי בִּהְיוֹת הַבֹּקֶר וַיְהִי קֹלֹת וּבְרָקִים וְעָנָן כָּבֵד עַל הָהָר וְקֹל שׁוֹפָר וְגוֹ׳. וַיְהִי קוֹל הַשֹּׁפָר וְגוֹ׳ וְהָאֱלֹהִים יַעֲנֶנּוּ בְקוֹל״.
segments.en: «What is his reward if he causes» the groom «to rejoice? «Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:» He is privileged» to acquire «the Torah, which was given with five voices, as it is stated: “And it was on the third day, when it was morning, there were sounds [kolot], and lightning and a thick cloud upon the mountain, and the voice of the shofar”» (Exodus 19:16). The plural kolot indicates at least two sounds, while “the voice of the shofar” is one more. The passage continues: «“And when the voice of the shofar» grew louder and louder, Moses spoke «and God answered him by a voice”» (Exodus 19:19). Along with the three previous voices, the second shofar and the voice with which God answered Moses amount to a total of five voices at the revelation at Sinai.

segments.he: אִינִּי? וְהָא כְּתִיב ״וְכׇל הָעָם רוֹאִים אֶת הַקּוֹלוֹת״!
segments.en: The Gemara asks: «Is this so? Isn’t it also written: “And the whole nation saw the voices» and the torches and the sound of the shofar” (Exodus 20:15)? Clearly more than five voices are mentioned with regard to the revelation at Sinai.

segments.he: אוֹתָן קוֹלוֹת, דְּקוֹדֶם מַתַּן תּוֹרָה הֲווֹ.
segments.en: The Gemara answers: «Those voices were» sounded «prior to the giving of the Torah,» so they are not included in this calculation of voices.

segments.he: רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ אָמַר: כְּאִילּוּ הִקְרִיב תּוֹדָה, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״מְבִאִים תּוֹדָה בֵּית ה׳״. רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק אָמַר: כְּאִילּוּ בָּנָה אַחַת מֵחוּרְבוֹת יְרוּשָׁלַיִם, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר ״כִּי אָשִׁיב אֶת שְׁבוּת הָאָרֶץ כְּבָרִאשׁוֹנָה אָמַר ה׳״.
segments.en: «Rabbi Abbahu said:» The reward for causing a groom to rejoice «is» the same «as if one had offered a thanks-offering» in the Temple, for «as it is stated» later in the previously cited verse from Jeremiah: «“Those who bring a thanks-offering to the house of the Lord.”» «And Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said:» The reward for causing a groom to rejoice is the same «as if one rebuilt one of Jerusalem’s ruins, as it is stated» later in the same verse: «“For I will restore the captivity of the land as it was in the beginning.”»

moves.summary: another dictum in the R' Ḥelbo–Rav Huna run: failing to gladden a groom whose feast one enjoys violates five voices
moves.about: the ruling that one who benefits from a groom's feast without gladdening him violates five voices

moves.summary: Jeremiah 33:11, whose five voices are counted off
moves.about: the five voices of Jeremiah 33:11 that such a person violates

moves.summary: and what is the reward of one who does gladden him?
moves.about: the reward earned by one who does gladden the groom, the converse of Rav Huna's penalty

moves.cueHe: אמר רבי יהושע בן לוי: זוכה לתורה
moves.summary: he merits the Torah, itself given with five voices, counted from Exodus 19:16 and 19:19
moves.about: one who gladdens the groom merits the Torah, which was itself given with five voices

moves.summary: but Exodus speaks of the people seeing the voices — so there were more than five
moves.about: whether the voices at Sinai were exactly five, given a verse that speaks of the people seeing further voices

moves.cueHe: אותן קולות, דקודם מתן תורה הוו
moves.summary: those voices preceded the giving of the Torah and are not counted; the biur marks the move with ומשיבים
moves.about: the voices of that verse preceded the giving of the Torah and so fall outside the count of five
